title: AMEX is Shutting Down Accounts...HERE'S WHY
actionable_recommendations: Form a corporation in your home state or one of the four anonymous states (Nevada, Wyoming, Delaware, New Mexico) to access business credit cards.
Obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) for your corporation to qualify for corporate credit cards.
Limit personal credit cards to five; use business credit cards afterward to protect personal credit scores.
When applying for a credit card, provide a monthly spending estimate that accurately reflects your needs.
claims_requiring_current_verification: American Express is shutting down accounts based on corporation status.
There are specific state websites that American Express uses to verify active corporations.
The maximum number of American Express cards one can hold is six.
intended_organization_or_user: Individuals seeking to maintain their American Express accounts and build credit.
major_ideas: Active management of your corporation is essential to retain credit card access.
Business credit cards generally do not affect personal credit scores unlike some personal cards.
American Express may offer new cards after bankruptcy if certain conditions are met.
prerequisites: Establish a corporation with an EIN.
Have a consistent source of income to justify the credit card limit.
proposed_workflow: Monitor your corporation's status on state websites regularly.
Apply for business credit cards after establishing your corporation and obtaining an EIN.
Once you receive offers, apply for business credit cards in a timely manner.
tools_templates_resources: Free credit dispute letters from GetDisputeLetters.com or SecretCreditLetters.com.
Legal support from NeverLoseInCourt.com for compliance issues.
Resources to manage and establish business credit can be found at TheCreditpreneur.com.
Credit application requirements include declaring expected monthly spending.
Documentation for compliance checks should be maintained for credit card applications.
